name: level1-lose-ecology
description:
Level 1 losing scenario: a massive blast with max krackle triggers ecology score collapse and, after a sustained 150-tick zero streak, the government shutdown that actually ends the level (ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS, EcologicalDisaster.ts). Rewritten for the Employee.ts morale fix (computeAverageMorale now filters to `employees.filter(e => e.alive)` before averaging, where it previously summed every roster entry including corpses): the file's own prior 4-round design was tuned against the PRE-fix behaviour, where a dead crew member's morale, frozen at whatever it was at death, diluted-but-never-cleared the average forever -- with the fix live, that whole problem stops existing (a dead employee is dropped from the average outright, the instant they die), so this file no longer needs the old design's massive 15-employee filler cushion refreshed every round, nor the fire-everyone-and-rehire-fresh dance between rounds that pre-fix corpse-dilution forced. Rebuilt from scratch as a single round: 4 parallel driller+drill_rig crews (employee #1's staffed:true rig plus 3 freshly hired/equipped ones) drill one 7x7-hole grid (49 holes, 2m spacing -- tight on purpose, see below) alongside 15 idle filler employees who never leave the depot. The blast (max krackle, 10kg, minimum 1.0m stemming) then kills all 4 active crew -- confirmed via state.damage.accidents, ~90m throw radius is unavoidable on this 96x96 map -- while driving ecology to exactly 0.

The key mechanic this redesign leans on, confirmed by direct probe and not previously documented in this file: once ecology clamps to exactly 0, it stays there completely unassisted. ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay only pulls a score that is strictly between 0 and 100 back toward the neutral 50 -- its own `value > 0` check excludes exactly 0 -- and nothing on this site (no building anywhere in BuildingDefs.ts carries an `ecology` scoreEffect, and the tick loop's own maxRecentVibration input is hardcoded to 0, events.ts) ever pushes it back up from there. So a single, sufficiently large blast reaching exactly 0 is enough to start (and guarantee) the full 150-tick shutdown countdown; the old design's second blast/round existed only to compensate for a first blast that undershot 0 (it reached 5.70, not 0, at the old file's own hole count and spacing) -- sizing the single blast correctly here removes the need for a second one entirely.

Two further engine quirks, confirmed by direct probe while investigating whether a living_quarters building could stabilize wellBeing here, turned out to make one actively counterproductive for this file's purposes -- noted here rather than fixed, since fixing either is out of this file's scope (scenario-JSON-only edit): (1) GameLoop.ts's completeRestForEmployee, the completion path for a living_quarters-serviced rest, calls replenishNeed with a single tick's own replenish rate (e.g. +8 fatigue for a Tier 1 building) regardless of how many ticks the rest itself took (2/3/8 depending on gauge) -- resting at a building this way replenishes LESS than resting in place with no building at all (which flatly restores the gauge to NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP=70 in one shot, EmployeeNeeds.ts's own documented design). (2) autoInsertNeedTasks (GameLoop.ts), unlike tickCollapse's own building search, never checks needRestSearchRadius before routing an employee toward the nearest living_quarters -- an employee routed toward a distant one spends the whole walk there counted as `isWorking` (needs drain at the faster "working" rate the entire trip, not the slower idle rate), often crashing them into an actual collapse before they arrive. Together these made every living_quarters placement tried here (near the depot, near the drill site, Tier 1, Tier 2) stall the 4 crews' drilling indefinitely rather than help -- confirmed repeatedly by direct probe -- so this file builds no buildings at all and instead leans on two things it can actually control: the 15-employee filler cushion (unaffected by either bug, since they are never routed anywhere) and a drilling phase short enough that even the filler's own slow, unavoidable idle-gauge decay (EmployeeNeeds.ts's idle drain rates, 0.5/tick each for hunger and fatigue) has not yet crashed their morale to the floor by blast time.

That last constraint is what the tight 2m hole spacing is actually for: confirmed by direct probe, the same 49-hole pattern at the old file's 3m spacing takes long enough to drill (~600+ ticks solo, ~360 with 4 crews at 3m) that the 15 filler's own morale has already crashed to 0 by the time the crew dies -- avgMorale stays pinned at 0 (filler-only, post-death) straight through the 150-tick shutdown window, and worker_revolt (REVOLT_TICKS=120) wins the race. At 2m spacing the same 4 crews finish the same 49 holes in 230 ticks with wellBeing still at 51.16 -- confirmed by direct probe, run twice for determinism -- so avgMorale is still meaningfully positive when the crew dies, and even though wellBeing does still crash to (and stay at) 0 for a stretch afterward (the filler's own decay catches up eventually regardless), that stretch starts late enough that ecological_shutdown's already-running 150-tick countdown (started at the blast) reaches its threshold first: worker_revolt's own ticksAtZero streak is only at 97 of the 120 it needs when shutdown claims levelEndReason at tick 380 -- a 23-tick margin, confirmed by direct probe, run twice for determinism (identical tick 380 / ecological_shutdown / cash outcome both times). events.ts's tick loop only ever sets levelEndReason on the FIRST condition to trip a given tick (bankruptcy, then ecological shutdown, then arrest, then revolt, each gated by `if (!state.levelEnded)`) -- once shutdown locks it in at tick 380, nothing later (including revolt's own counter, which was still climbing) can overwrite it.

steps.description: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- crews the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) with employee #1, the only qualified driller already on the roster.

Only vehicle #1 (drill_rig) is used this round -- the staffed roster's debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter would otherwise sit parked in the drill site's path: NavGrid pathing has no notion of "move aside", so a vehicle idling on a cell a drilling driller's route crosses blocks that route forever (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle, EntityMovementTick.ts) -- confirmed by direct probe, drilling stalls at a handful of holes indefinitely with these left in place, regardless of crew size.

Hiring a driller only grants the role's starting `blasting` qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION, Employee.ts) -- the drill_rig licence needed before any drill_hole action can be assigned to them comes from here. No UI equivalent: the player-facing path is `employee train` at a driving_center.

The assign row's own <select> (fleetDetailSections.ts's makeAssignRow) must be explicitly set to this employee before clicking Assign -- Assign reads whichever employee the <select> currently shows, which defaults to the first eligible (alive, licensed, not-yet-driving) one in roster order, not whichever employee this step names.

15 idle filler employees, never given a task: avgMorale (computeAverageMorale, Employee.ts) averages every ALIVE roster entry equally, so this cushion keeps it (and wellBeing derived from it, ScoreManager.updateScores) off the floor while the 4-crew round below drills and, later, dies in the blast -- once dead, the .alive filter drops them out of the average for good (the pre-fix bug this file used to work around: a dead employee's morale, frozen at whatever it was at death, used to drag the average down forever with no way to clear it).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:7 cols:7 spacing:2 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:5,5
steps.description: One decrement click on the strip's own spacing stepper (data-field="spacing", DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3 -> 2, Drill.ts) before dragging the SAME (5,5)-(17,17) box round1 always used: 7x7 holes at 2m spacing spans exactly the 12m this drag already covers (round((17-5)/2)+1=7), the same span 5x5 holes at the old 3m spacing covered (round(12/3)+1=5). Tight 2m spacing is not cosmetic -- confirmed by direct probe, it is what keeps 4 parallel crews finishing all 49 holes in ~230 ticks instead of ~600+: closer holes mean shorter drives between them, which is most of the difference between a crew that finishes with wellBeing still above 50 and one that has already crashed to 0 and cannot recover before the blast.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently misses events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s (#475), leaving them pending so later ticks halt and the run diverges while still passing command mode.

230 ticks (23 x tick 10, deterministic given the fixed seed and this exact command sequence) is enough for the 4 parallel driller+drill_rig crews to finish all 49 holes -- confirmed by direct probe, run twice for determinism (holeCount 49, wellBeing 51.16 both times).
Max krackle (10kg, the level's strongest available explosive) at minimum stemming (1.0m) -- catastrophic overcharge, exactly the file's own point.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

The catastrophic blast -- this file's whole point. ~90m throw radius is unavoidable on this map for anyone standing at the drill site, so all 4 active crew (employees #1, #6, #7, #8) die (deathCount 0->4); the 15 filler, who never left the depot, do not. Krackle vibration cuts ecology sharply in one blast, deterministically (no RNG in the blast->ecology formula, ScoreManager.ts's recordVibration) -- 49 holes at this spacing/charge produce enough projections (~5300, confirmed by direct probe) to clamp ecology to exactly 0, not merely low. That exact-0 clamp is what starts the government's countdown: applyDecay (ScoreManager.ts) only nudges a score that is strictly between 0 and 100 back toward 50 -- at exactly 0 (`value > 0` excludes it) it does nothing, and with no building anywhere on this site touching the ecology score and maxRecentVibration hardcoded to 0 in the tick loop (events.ts), nothing else ever will either. Ecology stays pinned at exactly 0 from this tick on, unassisted, for the full ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS=150 streak below -- one sufficiently large blast is enough; no second round is needed.

150 more ticks (15 x tick 10) after the blast -- ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS (EcologicalDisaster.ts). Ecology, pinned at exactly 0 since the blast above, reaches the sustained streak here; the government shutdown fires on the very last of these ticks (confirmed by direct probe, run twice for determinism: tick 380 both times). wellBeing recovers only partway (the surviving 15 filler's own morale has also been draining on pure idle-gauge decay since tick 0 -- REVOLT_TICKS=120 is close enough behind ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS=150 that this file's pacing is the whole point: worker_revolt's own ticksAtZero streak reaches only ~97 of the 120 it needs by the time shutdown locks the outcome in -- events.ts's tick loop sets levelEndReason on the FIRST condition to trip a given tick (bankruptcy, then ecological shutdown, then arrest, then revolt, each gated by `if (!state.levelEnded)`), so once shutdown claims it here, revolt's own later-arriving streak can never overwrite it.

expect.note: Final state confirms the government shutdown -- fired for real exactly ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS=150 after the single blast above, at tick 685 (up from 380, #554: charging is real work now -- the 49-hole charge order above, drained by its own wait step, pushes the blast itself, and everything timed from it, later by the same amount) -- and that worker_revolt's own, independently-running streak (still short of REVOLT_TICKS=120 at this point) never got the chance to overwrite it. cash stays comfortably positive throughout (never within remote reach of bankruptcy) -- the $5,000,000 starting cash in this file's own campaign-start command is headroom for direct, repeatable probing of the ecology/wellBeing pacing, not a requirement of the mechanic itself.
